thread:
sophie: heads up — ticket #48022 (AcmeSearch). They pinned a model in their Dedicated project and immediately started seeing embeddings fail. User paste:

```
POST /v1/embeddings
model: text-embed-1536-v2 (pinned)
input: ["batch of docs"]

Response 400:
{
  "error": "Embedding vector size mismatch: expected 1536, got 768"
}
```

They say reindex job hit this across many shards. Blocker for nightly ingest. :frowning:

eng-elena: can you grab the request-id and any proxy/runtime logs? Also check whether their Dedicated pool changed capacity recently.

sophie: request-id=01H9XY-req-3382. Proxy/runtime excerpt I pulled:

```
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z INFO request 01H9XY-req-3382 route=dedicated-pool-12 model=requested=text-embed-1536-v2
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z WARN runtime selection: no free instance for variant text-embed-1536-v2@fp16
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z INFO runtime fallback: selected text-embed-lite-768@q4_0 due to capacity
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z ERROR embedding_output: size=768 expected=1536 -> returning client error
```

Looks like runtime routed to a 768-dim variant and then the API returned the mismatch error.

ml-oncall-bot: quick triage checklist for runtime folks:
1) `GET /v1/models/text-embed-1536-v2` -> verify metadata.embedding_size == 1536
2) check response header `x-served-model-id` for the request to see what variant was used
3) inspect pool routing policy: is `allow_variant_fallback` enabled?

Expected metadata snippet (for reference):
```
{
  "id": "text-embed-1536-v2",
  "embedding_size": 1536
}
```

eng-elena: pulled catalog entry — embedding_size is 1536 as expected. Runtime logs show fallback to text-embed-lite-768@q4_0. Two possible root causes:
- pinned model only pins catalog/model id but runtime still allows cross-catalog fallbacks when `allow_variant_fallback=true`, or
- a compatibility-check bug where we compared name/tokenizer but not `embedding_size`, so 768 variant considered compatible.

runtime-oncall: confirmed it's a regression. PR #2419 relaxed variant compatibility checks and accidentally affected embeddings. The compatibility predicate no longer asserted `embedding_size` equality for fallback candidates. Hotfix: revert embedding relaxation and add explicit embedding_size check. Opened runtime PR 2527 and pushing to canary now.

product-ryan: customer comms options while we patch:
- Support can set `allow_variant_fallback=false` on their pool so routing will fail fast (503/NO_CAPACITY) instead of silently serving a wrong-dim variant.
- If customer accepts lower-dim embeddings temporarily, we can reindex to the 768 model (document relevance impact).
Which do we present?

sophie: I told the customer both. They prefer correctness over speed — asked us to block mismatched fallbacks. I set `allow_variant_fallback=false` on their pool. That made further ingestion attempts return capacity errors instead of dim-mismatch.

runtime-oncall: canary deploy at 2026-03-12T15:05:40Z (canary c-77). Test results:

```
# before fix: served-model-id=text-embed-lite-768@q4_0, embedding_len=768 -> client 400 mismatch
# after fix: no compatible instance -> 503/NO_CAPACITY (safer), or served-model-id=text-embed-1536-v2@fp16 if capacity available
```

rolling to prod now; full rollout ~8m.

sophie: customer reports reindex resumed at 2026-03-12T15:18:02Z. They confirmed embeddings now have length 1536 and the job completed. They asked for a short explanation we can share with them.

eng-elena: postmortem items:
- Add unit/integration tests to assert `embedding_size` equality for fallback candidates.
- Create alert if >1% embedding requests for a model return size-mismatch within 5m.
- Update docs about pinned-model semantics: pinned should guarantee dimensional compatibility; clarify runtime fallback behavior.

runtime-oncall: filed follow-ups RUNTIME-745 (hard constraint embedding_size), RUNTIME-746 (compatibility tests), OBS-312 (dim-mismatch alert). Planning expanded canaries tomorrow.

sophie: closing ticket with customer, attaching timeline and engineering tickets. Thanks all. :tada:
